title: Hadamard Product Factorization of the Riemann Zeta Function via the Completed Zeta ξ

problemStatement.formal: The completed zeta \xi(s) = \tfrac{1}{2} s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s) is an entire function of order 1, and admits the Hadamard product \xi(s) = e^{A+Bs}\prod_{\rho}(1 - s/\rho)e^{s/\rho} over the non-trivial zeros \rho of \zeta, with A = -\log 2 and B = -\sum_\rho \mathrm{Re}(1/\rho).
problemStatement.plain: The Riemann zeta function can be packaged into a symmetric entire function \xi whose only zeros are the non-trivial zeros of \zeta. Because \xi has order 1, Hadamard's factorization theorem expresses it as an exponential factor times an explicit infinite product over its zeros \rho, each contributing (1 - s/\rho)e^{s/\rho}. This is the analytic bridge from the location of zeros to prime counting.
whyMatters: It is the identity from which von Mangoldt's explicit formula for \psi(x) as a sum over zeros is derived, via the logarithmic derivative \zeta'/\zeta.
Every RH-conditional prime bound in the parent proof (\psi(x)=x+O(\sqrt{x}\log^2 x), the O(\sqrt{x}) Mertens bound) ultimately rests on the convergence of this product.
Formalizing the order-1 factorization would let several axioms in rh-consequences be derived rather than assumed.
